about.title: Visalia Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Visalia is the medical hub for much of Tulare County, so patients from across the region come here for surgeries, deliveries, imaging, and emergency treatment. Most of that care goes the way it should. Sometimes it does not, and the hard part is figuring out whether what happened was an unavoidable complication or a genuine breach of the standard of care. That distinction matters, because under California law a poor result by itself is not malpractice. Someone has to show that the provider did something a careful professional would not have done, and that the error caused real harm. These cases move on a clock set by MICRA: usually one year from the date you discovered the injury, and never more than three years from when it happened, with a 90-day notice sent to the provider before any lawsuit is filed. A qualified medical expert almost always has to weigh in. We handle medical malpractice claims and can review your records to explain your options.

whyChoose.title: What a Visalia Malpractice Case Requires

items.title: MICRA Deadlines Are Short
items.desc: California generally allows one year from the date you discovered the injury and no more than three years from the date it occurred. We can pin down which date applies to you before time runs out.

items.title: The 90-Day Notice Step
items.desc: Before a malpractice suit is filed in California, the provider must receive written notice at least 90 days in advance. Getting this right early keeps the claim on track.

items.title: Expert Review Comes First
items.desc: A bad outcome alone does not make a case; a qualified medical expert almost always has to confirm the standard of care was breached. We arrange that expert review on contingency, so there is no fee unless you recover.

items.question: I was treated in Visalia but live in a smaller Tulare County town. Does that change anything?
items.answer: No. Where you live does not affect your right to bring a claim, and the same California MICRA rules apply whether the care happened in Visalia or elsewhere in the county. We can meet with you by phone or video if traveling to Visalia is a burden.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: California caps non-economic damages, meaning things like pain and loss of enjoyment of life, and that cap increases every year under current law. Economic losses such as medical bills and lost income are handled separately. We can explain how the current figures apply to your situation without guessing at a number.

items.question: My surgery had a complication. Is that automatically malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Known complications can happen even when a surgeon does everything correctly, and California law only treats it as malpractice when the care fell below what a reasonably careful provider would have done. A medical expert reviewing your records is usually the only way to know which category your case falls into.
